facts.statement: Norellraptor lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Barremian to Aptian stages.
The type locality for Norellraptor is the Jiufotang Formation.
Norellraptor fossils were found in China.
Norellraptor is classified as a microraptorine dromaeosaurid.
The only known species of Norellraptor is Norellraptor barsboldi.
The genus is known from a single complete skeleton, specimen 130108-MHGU-F4281, which preserves plumage impressions.
facts.quote: known from a single complete skeleton including impressions of the plumage (specimen 130108-MHGU-F4281)

facts.statement: The complete Norellraptor skeleton measured approximately 57 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The whole skeleton measured approximately 57 cm long

facts.statement: The tail feathers of Norellraptor exhibited a rachis-dominated morphology.
facts.quote: the tail feathers were found to have a rachis-dominated morphology

facts.statement: Researchers believe the Norellraptor specimen was a post-juvenile when it died.
facts.quote: The specimen is believed to have been a post-juvenile upon its death

facts.statement: Norellraptor was assigned to the subfamily Microraptorini and is considered a sister taxon to Zhongjianosaurus.
facts.quote: From these findings, Norellraptor was assigned to Microraptorini, being a sister taxon to Zhongjianosaurus

facts.statement: The species name barsboldi honors the Mongolian paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold.
facts.quote: The specific epithet, barsboldi honours the late Rinchen Barsbold

facts.statement: Norellraptor lived in a temperate forested environment within the Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: Norellraptor lived in a temperate forested environment of the Jiufotang Formation

facts.statement: Norellraptor shared its environment with Sinotyrannus, Liaoconodon, Psittacosaurus, and various birds and pterosaurs.
facts.quote: It mainly lived alongside the tyrannosauroid Sinotyrannus, eutriconodont Liaoconodon, ceratopsian Psittacosaurus, and a wide assortment of enantiornithines, euornithines, and pterosaurs
